query: Should I add any bond exposure at all, or stay close to 100% equity given my horizon?

recommendations.title: Maintain Near 100% Equity Allocation - No Bond Exposure Needed
recommendations.summary: Given your aggressive risk tolerance, 15+ year horizon, high loss comfort (9/10), stable income, and strong emergency fund, maintaining a near 100% equity allocation is optimal for maximizing long-term wealth accumulation toward your FIRE goal.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your profile is ideal for minimal/zero bond exposure: (1) You're 30 with 15+ years until your FIRE target, providing ample time to recover from market downturns, (2) Your loss comfort score of 9/10 and aggressive risk tolerance indicate you can psychologically handle significant volatility, (3) Your stable $195K income with low debt and existing emergency fund means you won't need to liquidate investments during downturns, (4) Historical data shows 100% equity portfolios significantly outperform equity/bond mixes over 15+ year periods, (5) At your age, the opportunity cost of bonds (lower returns) substantially outweighs their volatility reduction benefits. Bonds typically make sense for capital preservation near retirement or for moderate/conservative investors - neither applies to you. Your current 85% equity + 5% crypto allocation is appropriate; the 10% cash serves as your volatility buffer.
recommendations.suggested_action: Continue current equity-focused strategy with no bond allocation

recommendations.title: Reduce Technology Sector Concentration Risk
recommendations.summary: Your 65% technology sector exposure creates significant concentration risk. Diversify into other high-growth sectors while maintaining aggressive equity stance to reduce volatility without sacrificing return potential.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: While tech has performed exceptionally well, your 65% tech concentration (QQQ, NVDA, GOOGL, META, AMZN, TSLA) exposes you to sector-specific risks that could derail your FIRE timeline. The 2022 tech drawdown saw many holdings drop 50-70%. Diversification into other sectors (healthcare, financials, industrials, international markets) can reduce portfolio volatility by 20-30% while maintaining similar long-term return expectations. Consider adding: VGT rotation into VTI (already held - increase weight), small-cap value (VBR/AVUV) for diversification premium, international developed (VEA/VXUS) to reduce US concentration, and emerging markets (VWO) for growth exposure. Target 40-45% tech maximum while adding 20% international, 15% small-cap value, keeping your aggressive equity profile intact.
recommendations.suggested_action: Gradually reduce tech concentration to 40-45%; add international and small-cap value exposure

recommendations.title: Optimize Cash Position for Maximum Growth
recommendations.summary: Your 10% cash allocation ($18K) exceeds necessary liquidity needs given your emergency fund status. Reduce to 2-3% and deploy excess into equities to accelerate FIRE goal achievement.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: You already have an emergency fund separate from this portfolio, stable income, and low liquidity needs. Holding 10% cash creates a significant drag on returns - at 8% equity returns vs 0.5% cash, that's ~$1,350 in annual opportunity cost, compounding to ~$44K over 15 years. Recommendation: Reduce cash to $3,600-5,400 (2-3%) for opportunistic rebalancing during market dips. This strategy maintains tactical flexibility while putting $12,600-14,400 to work immediately. Dollar-cost average this deployment over 3-6 months to mitigate timing risk. The small cash reserve enables you to buy during 10%+ corrections without selling winners, while the bulk of capital compounds. Given your high income and stable employment, you can replenish cash quickly if needed without portfolio liquidation.
recommendations.suggested_action: Reduce cash to 2-3%; deploy $12,600-14,400 into diversified equity ETFs over 3-6 months
recommendations.expected_return_range: Additional $35-45K over 15 years from deployed capital

recommendations.title: Reconsider Crypto Allocation Sizing
recommendations.summary: While 5% crypto aligns with aggressive risk tolerance, evaluate whether this allocation serves your FIRE goal or introduces unnecessary volatility without commensurate expected return improvement.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your $9K BTC position (5%) represents speculation rather than diversification. Analysis: (1) Crypto correlation with tech stocks has increased to 0.6-0.8 during drawdowns, failing to provide diversification when needed most, (2) Regulatory uncertainty creates tail risks that could impair your FIRE timeline, (3) BTC's risk-adjusted returns over full market cycles don't clearly exceed diversified equity portfolios, (4) The volatility (60-80% annualized) may not improve your risk-adjusted path to $2.5M vs adding to proven equity factors. Options: (A) Maintain 5% as 'high-risk speculation' allocation if you believe in crypto's long-term thesis and can tolerate potential 80%+ drawdown, (B) Reduce to 2-3% ($3,600-5,400) as 'lottery ticket' sizing, deploying difference to diversified equities, (C) Eliminate entirely, adding $9K to small-cap value or international exposure. Given your FIRE goal's importance and achievability through traditional equities alone, option B provides asymmetric upside exposure while limiting downside impact.
recommendations.suggested_action: Consider reducing crypto to 2-3% maximum; reassess necessity for FIRE goal achievement
